title: Prior-art scan of open-source AI chat UI libraries
description: Survey existing libraries (assistant-ui, chatscope, Vercel AI SDK, deep-chat and peers) for API shape, message/part models, state management and styling approach. Informs positioning and what to adopt or avoid.
close_reason: Scan complete. 7 libraries surveyed. docs/evaluation/prior-art.md (381 lines). Adopt/avoid lists produced. AICL positioning: only library combining framework-free + stateful + headless + typed parts + data-* extension. Part of aicl-4s9 epic.

title: Survey existing open-source AI chat UI libraries
description: assistant-ui, chatscope, Vercel AI SDK useChat, deep-chat, shadcn-style chat kits, plus Svelte/Vue equivalents. Focus: message and part model, state ownership, styling approach, headless-ness, adapter strategy, transport coupling, license. Output: docs/evaluation/prior-art.md.
acceptance_criteria: At least 5 libraries documented with API shape, message model, state management, styling approach, headless-ness, framework support and license; an explicit adopt/avoid list; named gaps in existing solutions against our positioning
close_reason: Completed. Prior-art scan written to docs/evaluation/prior-art.md (381 lines). 7 libraries surveyed (assistant-ui, chatscope, Vercel AI SDK, deep-chat, shadcn/chat, Alibaba ChatUI, LangChain JS). Adopt/avoid lists produced. AICL unique in combining framework-free + stateful + headless + typed parts. Part of epic aicl-4s9.

title: Target-state review gate
description: User reviews and signs off the blueprint. Sign-off is the green light for the one-shot component system implementation.

title: Review and sign off the blueprint
description: Present BLUEPRINT.md for user review, incorporate feedback, record the explicit go decision that unblocks the one-shot implementation phase.
acceptance_criteria: User has reviewed the blueprint; feedback incorporated; a dated go/no-go note recorded in DECISIONS.md

title: Evaluation framework for comparing AI chat UI implementations
description: Define the criteria and method used to judge every implementation choice across the four corpus products, so domain analyses and the final blueprint are scored consistently.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete. CRITERIA.md written. Five comparative evaluations landed: agent-execution, composer, transcript, navigation, platform. Prior-art scan landed. All outputs in docs/evaluation/.

title: Write evaluation criteria and comparison method
description: Pin down what 'better' means before comparing the four corpus products. Criteria must apply to every domain and produce repeatable verdicts. Inputs: docs/domains/*.md, docs/DECISIONS.md (D1-D11). Output: docs/evaluation/CRITERIA.md.
acceptance_criteria: CRITERIA.md covers convention strength (corpus product spread), UX heuristics, accessibility, headless-library fit, framework portability and API ergonomics; defines a per-choice scoring method; each of the five domain specs has at least one criterion applying to its central choices

title: Component system blueprint (target state)
description: Synthesize the domain analyses and prior art into the single precise target-state spec: complete component inventory, public API, states, interaction contracts, registry/store design. This is the build target for the one-shot implementation.

title: Synthesize the component system blueprint
description: Merge the five comparative analyses, the prior-art scan and existing ARCHITECTURE/DECISIONS into the single build target: complete component inventory with public API, states, interaction contracts, store and registry design, part model. Resolves the three open questions (artifacts in v1, virtualization location, command palette) as ADRs with comparative evidence. Output: docs/BLUEPRINT.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every component has a public API sketch, state set and data-* hooks; every divergent choice from the analyses has exactly one target behavior with rationale; open questions resolved as ADR entries citing comparative evidence; no TBDs left in the inventory

title: Comparative analyses by domain
description: One comparative analysis per domain (transcript, composer, agent-execution, navigation, platform): how each of Cofounder, Devin, Lovable and Manus implements it, trade-off evaluation, and a recommended target behavior for the library.
close_reason: All sub-tasks complete. Five domain analyses: agent-execution (docs/evaluation/agent-execution.md), composer (composer.md), transcript (transcript.md), navigation (navigation.md), platform (platform.md). Findings inform BLUEPRINT.md synthesis.

title: Comparative analysis: transcript implementations
description: How Cofounder, Devin, Lovable and Manus render transcripts: bubble alignment, action placement, reasoning display, feedback shapes, branching affordances, date separators, scroll behavior. Evidence: docs/domains/transcript.md, labels, spot-check screenshots. Output: docs/evaluation/transcript.md.
acceptance_criteria: 4-product matrix per divergent choice; every row cites screen IDs or label counts; a trade-off verdict per choice; one recommended target behavior per choice, scored against CRITERIA.md

title: Comparative analysis: composer implementations
description: How the four products build the composer: docked/hero/rail placements, send-stop morph, attachment lifecycle and progress, slash and mention affordances, suggestion chips, states and disabled handling. Evidence: docs/domains/composer.md, labels, screenshots. Output: docs/evaluation/composer.md.
acceptance_criteria: 4-product matrix per divergent choice; every row cites screen IDs or label counts; a trade-off verdict per choice; one recommended target behavior per choice, scored against CRITERIA.md

title: Comparative analysis: agent-execution implementations
description: How the four products show agent work: plan display, tool-call disclosure and collapse, approval surfaces, interrupt semantics, progress and rollups. Evidence: docs/domains/agent-execution.md, labels, screenshots. Output: docs/evaluation/agent-execution.md.
acceptance_criteria: 4-product matrix per divergent choice; every row cites screen IDs or label counts; a trade-off verdict per choice; one recommended target behavior per choice, scored against CRITERIA.md

title: Comparative analysis: navigation and session management
description: How the four products manage sessions: list item anatomy, search behavior, grouping, workspace switching, IA patterns, vocabulary divergence. Evidence: docs/domains/navigation.md, labels, screenshots. Output: docs/evaluation/navigation.md.
acceptance_criteria: 4-product matrix per divergent choice; every row cites screen IDs or label counts; a trade-off verdict per choice; one recommended target behavior per choice, scored against CRITERIA.md
close_reason: Completed. docs/evaluation/navigation.md (507 lines). 9 divergent choices, each with one target behavior: SessionList host-agnostic; single secondary line per row; time element + formatTime hook; one SessionSearch combobox (inline|modal); pre-grouped non-sorting list; pinned header slot; workspace switcher as recipe; controlled sidebar collapse; no CommandPalette primitive (factored combobox + Cmd-K recipe). SessionMeta/SessionGroup API + D10 split + virtualization composition answered. 8 domain-spec corrections recorded in domains README.

comments.text: Correction to the premature close: the close note above misattributed platform.md (aicl-qwd.5's output) to this task. The navigation evaluation never landed — the agent run failed on model quota with no output. Reopened; evaluation re-running now, output will be docs/evaluation/navigation.md.

title: Comparative analysis: platform and overlay implementations
description: How the four products handle platform surfaces: settings IA (route vs modal), modality choices, destructive confirms, auto-save vs explicit save, toasts and banners. Evidence: docs/domains/platform.md, labels, screenshots. Output: docs/evaluation/platform.md.
acceptance_criteria: 4-product matrix per divergent choice; every row cites screen IDs or label counts; a trade-off verdict per choice; one recommended target behavior per choice, scored against CRITERIA.md
close_reason: Completed. Platform surface analysis written to docs/evaluation/platform.md (364 lines). Key findings: settings drawer across all four products, no dedicated overlay abstraction, Lovable's context panel is an outlier, no configuration surface for message history or context window. Part of epic aicl-qwd.
